newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 29.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 29.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Tuesday:

* On Monday, U.S. stocks turned in a mixed performance, with the Dow Jones industrial average eking out another record while high-technology stocks fell. The 30-share Dow rose 7.67 points to 8,121.11, edging past the previous record of 8,116.93, set on Thursday. It was the Dow's fourth record in the past five sessions.

* Indonesian markets staged a marginal recovery on Monday as the crisis in regional currencies eased in the wake of Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's warning against speculation, dealers and brokers said.

* On Monday, Jakarta stocks ended flat as worries over the volatile rupiah appeared to ease after the currency generally strengthened against the dollar. The Jakarta composite index was up 0.76 points, or 0.11 percent, at the close at 710.82 points.
* On Tuesday, the rupiah was traded at 2,560.00/2,567.00 at 0205 GMT against an opening of 2,575.00/2,585.00
* Bank Niaga following an announcement on Monday that a privately-owned firm, PT Tunasmas Paduarta, planned to acquire a 50-percent stake in the bank, brokers said.

Tunasmas proposed to buy about a 40 percent stake in the bank from two major shareholders and a 10 percent stake from the public at a price of 8,000 rupiah per share, Lippo Securities said in an announcement. The firm is acting as underwriter for the offer.

* Transportation firm Steady Safe on a report in Bisnis Indonesia daily which quoted the chairman of Jakarta's public transportation association as saying that it will investigate the firm as its taxi fleet is suspected to be larger than that approved by government.
* Feedmill Anwar Sierad on market talk of a possible private placement, brokers said.

* Small property firm Mas Murni after Bisnis Indonesia quoted the company's president director Djaja Santosa as saying that it had signed an agreement to set up a joint-venture with Hong Kong-based Lintel Hospitality Consultants to develop its hotel business. He also said that the firm had targeted a profit growth of 20 percent for 1997.
* Property Royal Sentul Highlands on its encouraging debut on Monday.
* Tin miner Timah after announcement of a drop in its first half net profit.
* Bank Papan Sejahtera after the Jakarta stock exchange allowed it to resume trading on Monday after it was suspended on Friday.
* Bank BNI on a report in Bisnis Indonesia daily that it had completed the acquisition of Amsterdam-based Bank Indover.
